_exec_summary.SummaryText:
The accidental release prevention and emergency response policies:

Founded in 2011, Sila is a next-generation battery materials company with the mission to power the world. In 2023, Sila started the build-out of its first auto-scale plant in Moses Lake, WA (Facility), which began operations in September 2025.

Through focus, simplicity, and learning, Sila is committed to embedding health and safety into its business and managing its environmental footprint while striving to power the world's energy transition.

In addition to adhering to applicable federal, state, and local rules and regulations, it is Sila's policy to apply industry standards. As part of this commitment, Sila established a system to help ensure safe operation at the Facility including the prevention of accidental releases of hazardous substances. One component of this system is a Risk Management Program (RMP) that complies  with the requirements of the Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA) regulations under 40 CFR  Part 68. The Facility is also subject to the Occupational Safety & Health Administration's (OSHA) Process Safety Management (PSM) Standard, 29 CFR 1910.119.

The stationary source and regulated substances handled:

The Facility produces Titan Silicon, Silas breakthrough low swell Si/C silicon anode materials that drive lithium-ion battery performance enhancements for customer applications, including electric mobility, consumer electronics, drones, AR/VR, and satellites. Titan Silicon was launched in 2021 in the WHOOP 4.0 fitness wearable. The Facility contains the capacity needed to deliver for multiple automotive customers as well as a growing pipeline of customers. As demand grows for improved battery performance in everything from wearable devices and electric vehicles to drones and robotics, the Facility will serve a pivotal role in reducing U.S. reliance on foreign supply chains by ensuring a domestic supply of a critical material used in lithium-ion batteries.

With more than

250 patents filed and pending worldwide, Silas patent portfolio includes the core Intellectual Property (IP) enabling the low-swell silicon anode and the cell recipes used for deployment. This IP portfolio not only safeguards Silas innovation but also protects its partners investments for the long-term. Therefore, one of the raw materials used in the process is considered Confidential Business Information (CBI) and not included in the public version of the RMP.  While Sila employees and contractors operate under written confidentiality obligations, no safety information is withheld from them regarding the chemicals they work with, and the potential hazards associated with such chemicals. In additional to the confidential raw material referenced above, Sila also utilizes silane in the covered process, a flammable held at the Facility above the listed threshold quantity under the RMP regulation.

The general accidental release prevention program and chemical-specific prevention steps:

Sila implemented a combined Process Safety and Risk Management Program in line with the requirements of both RMP Program Level 3 and OSHA PSM. The Facility maintains a comprehensive PSM/RMP Manual that outlines its commitment to and compliance with each of the prevention program elements, emergency planning and response, hazard assessment, 5-year accident history, and submittal of the RMP.

At the core of the PSM/RMP Program, initial Process Hazard Analyses (PHA) were completed to identify potential hazards associated with the covered process operations as well as to evaluate the risk and adequacy of the engineered and administrative safeguards in place. The Facility also has an Inspection, Testing, and Preventative Maintenance Program in place to prevent failures of the covered equipment and safeguards as identified in the PHA.

The Facilitys operations team participated in PHAs, commissioning, and pre-startup activities for the Facility, was instrumental in the development of the

preparation.

Planned changes to improve safety:

The team at the Facility continually evaluates and, as applicable, implements corrective actions resulting from process safety activities e.g., PHAs, incident investigations, and compliance audits. Sila also fosters a reporting culture (including anonymous reporting) and shares lessons learned across the organization.

The Facility is designed in accordance with the recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices to protect employees, the community, and the environment. Future changes to the Facility will be reviewed and implemented through the MOC process.
